introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

The paper contains eight questions.

Question 2(b) : « directly from P to Q » est interprété comme le trajet de P vers Q en passant par O (durée pi/3 s).

questions.enonce_markdown: The equation of motion of a particle $P$ moving in a straight line $OX$ is $3\dfrac{d^2x}{dt^2} + 6\dfrac{dx}{dt} + 4x = 0$, where $x$ is the displacement of $P$ from $O$ at time $t$. Initially, $P$ is at $O$, moving with speed $\sqrt{3}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Show that the displacement $x$ of $P$ can be written in the form $x = Ae^{-t}\cos(nt+\varepsilon)$, stating the values of $A$, $n$ and $\varepsilon$. *[7 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Auxiliary equation.** Try $x = e^{\lambda t}$ in $3\ddot{x}+6\dot{x}+4x=0$:

$$3\lambda^2+6\lambda+4=0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \lambda=\frac{-6\pm\sqrt{36-48}}{6} = -1\pm\frac{\sqrt{12}}{6}\,i = -1\pm\frac{i}{\sqrt{3}}.$$

The roots are complex (light damping), so

$$x = e^{-t}\left(C\cos nt + D\sin nt\right),\qquad n=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}},$$

which can be written $x = Ae^{-t}\cos(nt+\varepsilon)$.

**Initial conditions.** At $t=0$, $x=0$:

$$A\cos\varepsilon = 0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \varepsilon = \pm\frac{\pi}{2}.$$

Differentiate:

$$\dot{x} = Ae^{-t}\left[-\cos(nt+\varepsilon) - n\sin(nt+\varepsilon)\right].$$

At $t=0$ with $\cos\varepsilon=0$: $\dot{x}(0) = -An\sin\varepsilon = \sqrt{3}$, so $A\sin\varepsilon = -\sqrt{3}\cdot\sqrt{3} = -3$.

Taking the amplitude $A>0$ forces $\sin\varepsilon=-1$, that is $\varepsilon=-\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, and then $A=3$.

$$\boxed{A=3,\qquad n=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3},\qquad \varepsilon=-\frac{\pi}{2}}$$

Therefore $x = 3e^{-t}\cos\left(\dfrac{t}{\sqrt{3}}-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 3e^{-t}\sin\dfrac{t}{\sqrt{3}}$.

*Check:* $x(0)=0$ and $\dot{x}(0)=3\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\sqrt{3}$ m s$^{-1}$ as required.

questions.enonce_markdown: The equation of motion of a particle $P$ moving in a straight line $OX$ is $3\dfrac{d^2x}{dt^2} + 6\dfrac{dx}{dt} + 4x = 0$, where $x$ is the displacement of $P$ from $O$ at time $t$. Initially, $P$ is at $O$, moving with speed $\sqrt{3}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Find the period of the motion. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The motion is $x = 3e^{-t}\cos(nt+\varepsilon)$ with $n=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$. The oscillation repeats its zero crossings every time $nt$ increases by $2\pi$, so

$$T=\frac{2\pi}{n}=2\pi\sqrt{3}\ \mathrm{s}\approx 10.9\ \mathrm{s}.$$

(This is the period of the damped oscillation; the amplitude itself decays by the factor $e^{-T}$ in each period.)
themes: simple harmonic motion of a particle

questions.enonce_markdown: A particle performs simple harmonic motion with centre $O$ and amplitude $2$ metres. The period of oscillation is $\pi$ seconds. $P$ and $Q$ are two points which lie at a distance $\sqrt{3}\ \mathrm{m}$ on either side of $O$. Find the time taken by the particle to move directly from $P$ to $Q$. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Angular frequency.** The period is $\pi$ s, so $\omega=\dfrac{2\pi}{\pi}=2\ \mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}$. With amplitude $a=2$ m and centre $O$, take the time origin when the particle passes $O$:

$$x = 2\sin 2t.$$

**Time from $O$ to $Q$.** $x=\sqrt{3}$ when

$$2\sin 2t=\sqrt{3}\ \Longrightarrow\ \sin 2t=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\ \Longrightarrow\ 2t=\frac{\pi}{3}\ \Longrightarrow\ t=\frac{\pi}{6}\ \mathrm{s}$$

(first time, taking the smallest positive value).

**Directly from $P$ to $Q$.** $P$ is at $x=-\sqrt{3}$ and $Q$ at $x=+\sqrt{3}$, symmetric about $O$. Moving directly from $P$ to $Q$ the particle passes through $O$ once, with equal times on each side:

$$t_{PQ}=2\times\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi}{3}\ \mathrm{s}\approx 1.05\ \mathrm{s}.$$

*Check with the speed formula:* at $x=\sqrt{3}$, $v^2=\omega^2(a^2-x^2)=4(4-3)=4$, so $|v|=2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, consistent with $\dot{x}=4\cos 2t=4\cos\frac{\pi}{3}=2$.
themes: simple harmonic motion of a particle
